html:
The main residence of the emperors of Constantinople for about 800 years, begun by Constantine around 330. It spread down terraces between the Hippodrome and the Sea of Marmara, next to Hagia Sophia.

It was not one building but a walled town of halls, courts, chapels, baths, gardens and barracks, rebuilt and added to by emperor after emperor. Here the court of the Byzantine Empire ran its slow, splendid ceremonies, which foreign visitors described with wonder. The palace had its own church and harbour and a gallery linking it to the emperor's box at the races.

From the 1080s the emperors lived mostly in the Blachernae palace at the north end of the city. The Great Palace decayed, was looted in the crusader sack of 1204, and was a ruin by 1453. Little survives but foundations and a large floor mosaic, now in a museum.
sum: The main residence of the emperors of Constantinople for about 800 years, begun by Constantine around 330. It spread down terraces between the Hippodrome and the Sea of Marmara, next to Hagia Sophia.
